newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec paper endorses separatist Bloc Quebecois.
newsitem.headline: Quebec paper endorses separatist Bloc Quebecois.

text.p: The influential Montreal French-language newspaper Le Devoir endorsed the separatist Bloc Quebecois in an editorial on Wednesday ahead of the June 2 election.
"The Bloc Quebecois, for the principle," said the editorial headline.
News Editor Lise Bissonnette said the paper could not support Prime Minister Jean Chretien's Liberals or Jean Charest's Conservatives because of their tough stand on Quebec.
Le Devoir said the Bloc was the least worst choice, because it was defending Quebec aspirations in Ottawa.
"Since we are heading toward another referendum, the reasons behind the election of a separatist presence in Ottawa in the 1993 election still stand," it said.
The Bloc Quebecois won 54 of Quebec's 75 seats in the 1993 election and formed the official opposition in the last parliament.
